chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I was performing tawaf around the House when suddenly a man was saying: Why is it that these two corners are touched, while these two are not touched? So I said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم touched these two and did not approach these two, so do not approach them when the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not approach them. Jamil said: And I saw Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام touching all of the corners. So there is no contradiction between these two reports and the first report, because both of them contain the account of the action of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. And it is possible that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not touch them because in touching them there is not the same merit and encouragement toward reward as there is in touching the Iraqi Corner and the Yemeni Corner. And he did not say that touching them is prohibited or disliked. For this reason, Jamil related that he saw Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام touching all of the corners; and had it not been permissible, he عليه السلام would not have done it.

key_terms.الْبَيْتِ: the Ka'bah, around which tawaf is performed
key_terms.الْعِرَاقِيِّ: the Iraqi Corner of the Ka'bah
key_terms.الْفَضْلِ: special merit or excellence in the act
key_terms.الْيَمَانِيِّ: the Yemeni Corner of the Ka'bah
key_terms.يُسْتَلَمَانِ: are touched by hand during tawaf

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to touch all the corners of the Ka'bah during tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on touching the corners of the Ka'bah during tawaf. It indicates that the Iraqi and Yemeni corners carry special merit based on the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, while touching the other corners remains permissible and is not prohibited or disliked, as shown by the practice of Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام.
